## Pull request overview

Adds a development toolchain to the ObjectStack monorepo by expanding `@objectstack/cli` with new commands (serve/dev/doctor/create), adding repo-level pnpm shortcuts, and documenting the intended workflows.

**Changes:**
- Added new CLI commands: `serve`, `dev`, `doctor`, and `create` (plugin/example scaffolding).
- Updated repo scripts (`pnpm doctor`, `pnpm setup`, `pnpm test`, etc.) and added new developer docs (`DEVELOPMENT.md`, `TOOLCHAIN_DEMO.md`).
- Updated dependencies/lockfile to support server startup and plugin loading.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 10 out of 11 changed files in this pull request and generated 17 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| pnpm-lock.yaml | Adds workspace deps for CLI to use core + hono server plugin. |
| packages/cli/package.json | Adds `@objectstack/core` + `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` dependencies for new commands. |
| packages/cli/src/bin.ts | Registers new CLI commands and updates CLI metadata/version. |
| packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts | Implements `objectstack serve` for starting a kernel and optionally an HTTP server plugin. |
| packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts | Implements `objectstack dev` wrapper around `pnpm --filter ... dev`. |
| packages/cli/src/commands/doctor.ts | Implements `objectstack doctor` environment checks. |
| packages/cli/src/commands/create.ts | Implements `objectstack create` scaffolding for plugin/example templates. |
| package.json | Adds repo-level `doctor`, `setup`, `test` shortcuts. |
| README.md | Updates quickstart to include `pnpm doctor` and links to development guide. |
| DEVELOPMENT.md | Adds development/debugging/testing guide and CLI usage docs. |
| TOOLCHAIN_DEMO.md | Demonstrates the new tooling and intended workflows. |
</details>

The core kernel API uses `use(plugin)` to register plugins (see `packages/core/src/kernel.ts:34`), but this command calls `kernel.registerPlugin(...)`, which doesn’t exist. Switch to the correct registration method (and consider failing fast if a required plugin can’t be registered).

The generated plugin template imports/implements the runtime `Plugin` interface, but its `package.json` template doesn’t depend on `@objectstack/core` (which is where the runtime `Plugin` interface used by existing plugins lives). Add `@objectstack/core` as a dependency (like `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/package.json`) and align the template’s imports accordingly.

The generated `src/index.ts` template won’t type-check against the actual plugin lifecycle: `@objectstack/spec` does not export `Plugin` at the root (see `packages/spec/src/index.ts`), and the runtime plugin interface expects `init(ctx)` (required) / `start?(ctx)` / `destroy?()` (see `packages/core/src/types.ts:65`). Update the template to import `Plugin` (and `PluginContext` if needed) from `@objectstack/core` (or `@objectstack/spec/contracts` if you intend the contracts interface), and rename `initialize` → `init` (and optionally add `start`).

The template sets the plugin `name` to the raw project name (e.g. `auth`), but existing runtime plugins use a reverse-domain style identifier (e.g. `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:8` → `com.objectstack.engine.objectql`, `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/hono-plugin.ts:17` → `com.objectstack.server.hono`). Using short names increases the chance of collisions. Consider generating a reverse-domain-style id by default (or at least documenting/enforcing uniqueness).

`execSync()` is invoked with a shell command string that interpolates the user-provided `packageName` into `--filter @objectstack/${packageName}`. This allows shell injection if `packageName` contains characters like `;`/`&&`. Prefer `spawn`/`execFile` with an argument array (no shell), and validate `packageName` against an allowlist regex (e.g., `^[a-z0-9-]+$` or `all`).

The core kernel lifecycle methods are `bootstrap()` / `shutdown()` (or `destroy()`), not `boot()`. As written, `kernel.boot()` will throw. Update to the correct lifecycle call for the kernel class you instantiate.
```suggestion
      await kernel.bootstrap();
```

`parseInt(options.port)` is not validated; non-numeric values will produce `NaN` and may lead to confusing failures when constructing the server plugin. Parse the option via Commander’s option arg parser (or validate after parsing) and error out with a clear message if the port is invalid/out of range.

`name` is used directly to build package names, directories, and TS identifiers (via `toCamelCase`), but there’s no validation/sanitization. Inputs like `my_plugin`, `my plugin`, or `123` can generate invalid package.json names or invalid TS identifiers in the generated source. Validate `name` up front (e.g., enforce kebab-case and ensure the derived identifier is a valid JS identifier), and fail with a clear error message if it’s not.

PR description says the new docs are English-only, but this file starts with a Chinese title and includes a Chinese section link. Either update the PR description or adjust the document to match the stated English-only documentation goal.

This doc claims the `serve` command has “Hot-reload support”, but the implementation in `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` just loads the config once and boots the kernel; there’s no file watching/restart logic. Either remove the hot-reload claim or implement config/plugin reload behavior.
```suggestion

```

`name` is interpolated into `projectName` and then passed to `path.join(...)` without sanitizing path separators. Inputs like `../../evil` can cause the normalized `targetDir` to escape the intended `packages/plugins` or `examples` base directory. Reject names containing `/` or `\` (and `..` segments) before building paths, or normalize and verify `targetDir` stays within the expected base dir.

The link `[中文](#中文版)` points to an anchor that doesn’t exist in this document (there’s no `# 中文版` section). Either add the referenced section or remove/update the link to avoid broken navigation.
```suggestion
> **English** | 中文
```

In the generated example template, the `dev` script is `tsx watch objectstack.config.ts`, but `objectstack.config.ts` only exports a stack definition and has no side effects—so this “dev” command will just exit immediately (and keep re-running on changes without doing anything). Consider changing the template’s dev workflow to something actionable (e.g., `objectstack compile` in watch mode if supported, or `objectstack serve` if the goal is to run a server).
```suggestion
          dev: 'objectstack compile',
```

`--no-server` currently only skips *auto*-registering `HonoServerPlugin`, but plugins from `config.plugins` are always registered. If a user includes `new HonoServerPlugin(...)` in `config.plugins`, `--no-server` won’t actually run headless. Consider either filtering out known HTTP server plugins when `--no-server` is set, or clarifying the flag’s behavior in the help text/docs.
